key_insight: HorizonStream introduces a horizon-aware attention mechanism that adapts influence over time, letting a streaming 3D reconstruction model preserve short-lived correspondences while maintaining persistent global structure under strict causal and bounded-memory constraints.
problem_solved: Mitigates drift, jitter and collapse in online (streaming) 3D reconstruction by addressing the mismatch between uniform attention patterns and the inherently temporally heterogeneous evidence in long sequences.
method: Horizon-aware attention: allocate attention strength by temporal ‘horizons’ so recent, mid-range, and long-range evidence get different, learned influence patterns.
Streaming architecture with bounded memory: maintain a compact memory bank and causal update rules to support long-horizon reasoning without unbounded storage.
Efficient implementation: multi-scale temporal windows and lightweight aggregation to keep per-frame compute and latency low for real-time use.
impact: Enables more stable, drift-resistant online mapping and pose estimation for robotics, AR/VR, and autonomous systems, improving reliability on long deployments while respecting latency and memory limits.

paper_title: HorizonStream: Long-Horizon Attention for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Chong Cheng, Peilin Tao, Nanjie Yao, Guanzhi Ding, Xianda Chen
